columns.label: Realms
columns.definition: Lua run in the server (S), client (C) and menu (M) realm. yes = arbitrary Lua with its result; partial = only through console commands, fixed tools, without a result, or once the user writes the game side; no = not reachable.

columns.label: Errors
columns.definition: Lua errors raised anywhere in the game (not only by the call) are captured and readable through a tool. partial = only through the console log or a console capture.

columns.label: Hot reload
columns.definition: Run an edited file again in the running game without a map change. partial = limited (agent code only, one file include, or a redeploy).

columns.label: Ents
columns.definition: Dedicated tools to find and inspect entities and players. partial = a subset (players, status, what is near the player). Generic Lua execution does not count.

columns.label: Traces
columns.definition: Raycasts from an arbitrary origin. partial = only from the player's view.

columns.label: Screenshot
columns.definition: Screenshot from an arbitrary viewpoint (position and angles). partial = player view, window or region only.

columns.label: Hooks
columns.definition: List hooks and trace or instrument their calls. partial = only one of the two, waiting for a hook, or tracing functions.

columns.label: Perf
columns.definition: Profiling of game code. partial = snapshot counters, timing of traced calls, optional profiler, or static analysis without the game.

columns.label: Jobs
columns.definition: Long Lua work run in the background with status and result. partial = a deferred run, bounded waits, or listeners of a host project.

columns.label: Tests
columns.definition: Automated tests run inside the game. partial = assertion suites without a test runner, or tests against a mocked engine.

columns.label: Multi-inst.
columns.definition: Several games driven at once from one MCP server. partial = pick one server or process among several, without coordination.

columns.label: Debugger
columns.definition: Breakpoints with stepping and locals.

columns.label: Input
columns.definition: Player input injected in the engine (CreateMove, StartCommand, engine +commands). partial = OS-level input (SendKeys, xdotool) that takes the real keyboard and mouse.

columns.label: Pure Lua
columns.definition: No native code runs inside the game process: the game side is Lua only, or there is no game side.

columns.label: Auth
columns.definition: yes = token/secret required, or no network listener at all. no = a listener that accepts calls without a required secret.

columns.label: No inject
columns.definition: yes = no DLL injection, remote thread or process memory write into the game (loading a module through the game's own require is not injection).

columns.label: Dedicated
columns.definition: Works with a dedicated server (srcds). partial = limited there.

columns.label: Linux
columns.definition: Works with Garry's Mod or srcds on Linux. partial = only part of the tool works there.

columns.label: 1-step install
columns.definition: yes = one command (plugin install, npx, extension install) plus at most copying files into the game; partial = several manual steps or an injector; no = the user must build it from source or write the game side first.

columns.label: Long calls
columns.definition: yes = MCP Tasks, or progress notifications + cancellation with no blocking server-side timeout <= 30 s on game work; no = a blocking timeout <= 30 s cuts the call, or neither progress nor cancellation; partial = progress without cancellation or vice versa.

columns.label: MCP spec
columns.definition: yes = declares protocol version >= 2025-06-18, handles notifications/cancelled, returns structuredContent with outputSchema; partial = 1-2 of 3; no = none. SDK-based servers are credited with what their pinned SDK does.

columns.label: Own CI
columns.definition: yes = the repository's CI runs its tests; partial = CI only builds or publishes; no = no CI workflow.

columns.label: License
columns.definition: yes = LICENSE file present; no = no license file (all rights reserved by default).

columns.label: Agent feedback
columns.definition: yes = the tool itself invites the agent to report friction and that report is collected (gmod-mcp: plugin option feedback_offers, agent-feedback issues); no = nothing in the tool asks for it.
